items.title: Min Aung Hlaing wins parliamentary vote to become Myanmar president

featured_image.name: Myanmar's General Min Aung Hlaing set to become president - Yahoo

items.description:
Myanmar's former military chief Min Aung Hlaing was elected president on Friday by the country's junta-installed parliament, completing a transition five years in the making from coup leader to nominal civilian head of state. The 69-year-old general, who seized power in 2021 by ousting the democratically elected government of Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, won the presidency in a bicameral vote that was widely seen as a foregone conclusion, with pro-military lawmakers controlling roughly 86 percent of parliamentary seats.[1][2]

The vote, held at 10:00 a.m. local time in the capital Naypyidaw, saw members of both legislative chambers choose from among three vice-presidential candidates: Min Aung Hlaing, Nan Ni Ni Aye of the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party, and former Prime Minister U Nyo Saw, a retired lieutenant general and close Min Aung Hlaing ally. Union Parliament Speaker U Aung Lin Dwe had confirmed on Thursday that all three candidates met the constitutional qualifications for the presidency.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: U.S. Embassy urges Americans to leave Lebanon over Iran university threats

featured_image.name: Iran threatens US, Israel-linked universities across Middle East

items.description:
The U.S. Embassy in Beirut issued an urgent security alert on Friday urging all American citizens to depart Lebanon while commercial flights remain available, warning that Iran and its allied militias "may intend to target universities in Lebanon."[1][2]

The advisory described the security environment as "volatile and unpredictable," citing ongoing airstrikes, drone activity, and rocket fire across the country, particularly in southern Lebanon, the Beqaa region, and parts of Beirut. "Iran has specifically threatened American universities across the Middle East," the embassy said, though it did not identify any specific institutions at risk.[2][3][4]

items.title: Pakistan faces LNG crisis as Iran war chokes Asian economies

featured_image.name: How war on Iran turned Pakistan's LNG surplus into a looming ...

items.description: Five weeks into the conflict triggered by joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is sending economic shockwaves far beyond the Middle East, with Asian economies bearing the brunt of what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."[1]

items.title: North Korea razes villages near key missile launch site

featured_image.name: North Korea rebuilding Sohae rocket launch site, say observers

items.description: North Korea has demolished two villages near its main satellite and missile launch facility and tested an upgraded solid-fuel rocket engine, developments that analysts say point to an accelerating weapons buildup as the United States remains consumed by its military campaign in the Middle East.

items.title: Iran refuses ceasefire talks as U.S. jet downed over Iran

featured_image.name: US F-15E fighter jet shot down over Iran

items.description: Diplomatic efforts to end the five-week-old war between the United States and Iran unraveled on Friday as Tehran formally refused to participate in talks proposed for Islamabad, and Qatar confirmed it would not serve as lead mediator — leaving regional powers scrambling to find a new path to negotiations even as the conflict escalated with the first downing of a U.S. combat aircraft over Iranian territory.

items.title: Italy extends fuel tax cut as Iran war strains global economies

featured_image.name: The Italian government plans to extend the reduced excise tax on fuel —  Bloomberg | UA.NEWS

items.description: Just over a month into the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, the economic fallout is rippling far beyond the Middle East, battering energy-dependent economies in Asia and straining European fiscal frameworks. South Korea and Japan, both heavily reliant on Persian Gulf energy imports, have emerged as the non-combatant nations bearing the heaviest burden, while European governments scramble to shield households from surging fuel costs.

items.title: U.S. jet shot down over Iran as bridge strike death toll rises to 13

featured_image.name: US F-15E fighter jet shot down over Iran

items.description:
A U.S. airstrike on Thursday destroyed the B1 bridge in Iran's Alborz province, a 136-meter structure that was the tallest bridge in the Middle East, killing at least eight people and wounding 95 others, according to Iranian officials. The death toll later climbed to 13 by Friday, Iranian state media reported.[1][2][3][4][5]

The strike marks a sharp escalation in the targeting of Iranian civilian infrastructure as Operation Epic Fury, which began on February 28, enters its fifth week.[6][7]

items.title: Iran drone strike on Riyadh embassy far worse than disclosed

featured_image.name: Iran targets U.S. allies, hits American Embassy in Riyadh - Axios

items.description: The March 3 Iranian drone strike on the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, caused far more destruction than the American and Saudi governments publicly acknowledged, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing current and former U.S. officials. Multiple floors of the embassy were heavily damaged, parts of the building remain "unrecoverable," and a fire sparked by the attack burned for twelve hours — a stark contrast to the Saudi Defense Ministry's initial assessment of "limited fire and minor material damage".[1][2][3]

items.title: Gaza Christians mark Good Friday as ceasefire strains

featured_image.name: Christian faithful gather in Gaza City to mark Good Friday

items.description:
Gaza City’s Christian community gathered at the Holy Family Church on Friday to mark Good Friday, a subdued observance that came as the enclave’s ceasefire with Israel remained in place but under strain. The service followed Palm Sunday celebrations at the same church less than a week earlier, one of the clearest signs that Holy Week rites have resumed in Gaza after long disruption from war.[1][2][3][4][5]

The prayers unfolded against a backdrop of continuing insecurity. Reuters reported on March 31 that Gaza health officials said Israeli fire had killed at least 700 people since the ceasefire took hold, while the Associated Press has described the truce as tenuous and marked by near-daily violence. That has left Gaza’s remaining Christians celebrating Easter season with caution rather than relief.[2][6][4][5]

items.title: U.S. tells Israel Iran negotiations have hit a deadlock

featured_image.name: Iran Oil Revenue Soars as It's the Only Exporter Out of Hormuz

items.description: Five weeks into the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, the conflict's cascading economic and humanitarian toll is reshaping energy markets, stranding thousands of mariners, and frustrating diplomatic efforts to bring fighting to an end. On Friday, the U.S. informed Israel that negotiations with Iran had hit a deadlock, even as tentative signs of resumed commercial shipping offered a sliver of hope in the otherwise shuttered Strait of Hormuz.[1]

items.title: German FM warns Trump's NATO exit threat risks alliance

featured_image.name: New German Foreign Minister Wadephul Pledges Stronger EU ...

items.description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has publicly expressed alarm over President Donald Trump's latest threat to pull the United States out of NATO, calling the alliance of "enormous importance" to Germany and all its members as a widening transatlantic rift over the Iran conflict rattles European capitals.

items.title: Satellite images confirm Iran damaged $136M US radar in Saudi Arabia

featured_image.name: Satellite images show US AN/TPY-2 radar damaged in March 1 ...

items.description: New satellite imagery has confirmed that an Iranian strike on March 1 damaged a U.S. AN/TPY-2 radar system at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, according to CNN reporting published this week. The radar is a core component of the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) missile interception system, one of the most advanced missile-tracking platforms in the American arsenal.[1]

items.title: French, Japanese ships cross Hormuz in first Western transits since Iran war

featured_image.name: Container ship declaring French ownership passes through Strait of ...

items.description: A French-owned container ship and a Japanese-linked LNG tanker crossed the Strait of Hormuz this week, marking the first transits by Western European and Japanese vessels since Iran imposed a near-total blockade of the waterway following U.S.-Israeli strikes on February 28.

items.title: Doctors Without Borders confirms Gaza supply shutdown since January

featured_image.name: Gaza: Medical care under fire | Doctors Without Borders - USA

items.description:
Doctors Without Borders warned this week that Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza have pushed healthcare services to a breaking point, with the organization unable to bring any medical supplies into the territory since January 1.[1][2]

In a testimony published on the MSF website on April 3, Dr. Randa Abu El-Khair Masoud, the organization's project medical referent in Gaza, said nearly 50 percent of essential chronic medications are critically low, including treatments for diabetes, hypertension, thyroid conditions, and respiratory diseases. MSF has already stopped accepting new patients for its non-communicable disease services, limiting care to existing patients.[1]

"The needs in Gaza are massive, yet not enough aid is entering because Israeli authorities are blocking it. Just outside of Gaza, there are trucks with food and medicine waiting, yet they are blocked," Masoud said.[1]

items.title: Investors tune out Trump as Iran war roils energy markets

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-FRANCE-ENERGY-OIL-WAR-IRAN-US-ISRAEL

items.description: More than a month after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes, the global fallout from the conflict is rippling far beyond oil prices — threatening critical helium supplies, rattling semiconductor manufacturers, and accelerating the world's pivot toward renewable energy.

items.title: Iranian cluster missiles hit Haifa area as war nears sixth week

featured_image.name: What are Iran's cluster munitions that are penetrating Israeli defences?

items.description:
Iran launched ballistic missiles armed with cluster munitions at northern Israel on Friday morning, striking multiple sites in the Haifa area and wounding at least one person as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran entered its 35th day with no signs of abating.

A 79-year-old man was lightly wounded by cluster munition debris after an Iranian ballistic missile struck a home in Kiryat Ata, near Haifa, according to the Times of Israel and the Jerusalem Post. Emergency services responded to at least 10 impact sites across Haifa and surrounding towns, where damage was reported to roads and vehicles. The IDF assessed that the Iranian missiles were equipped with cluster munition warheads, which scatter explosive submunitions over wide areas.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Three charged over arson attack on Jewish ambulances in London

featured_image.name: Three more people arrested in Golders Green ambulance attack ...

items.description: British prosecutors have charged three people following the arson attack that destroyed four Jewish volunteer ambulances in Golders Green, north London, on March 23. Hamza Iqbal, 20, and Rehan Khan, 19, both British nationals from Leyton in east London, along with a 17-year-old boy — a dual British and Pakistani national from Walthamstow — each face a charge of arson being reckless as to whether life would be endangered. The three are set to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday, April 4.[1][2][3]

items.title: Earthquake kills 8 in Afghanistan, tremors felt across South Asia

featured_image.name: Eight dead after earthquake of magnitude 5.9 strikes ...

items.description:
A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region on Friday, killing at least eight people when a house collapsed on the outskirts of Kabul, authorities said.

The victims were all members of the same family, according to Hafizullah Basharat, a spokesman for the Kabul governor, who said a child was also injured in the collapse in the capital's Bagrami district. Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority confirmed the casualties.[1][2]

items.title: Zelenskyy accuses Russia of 'Easter escalation' after massive daytime strike kills six

featured_image.name: Zelensky accuses Russia of 'buying time' to stall truce talks

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday accused Russia of an "Easter escalation" after Moscow launched nearly 500 drones and cruise missiles at Ukrainian cities in broad daylight, killing at least six people, even as the two sides negotiate a prisoner-of-war exchange ahead of Orthodox Easter on April 12.

items.title: US intel finds Iran unlikely to negotiate on Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: How US-Israel attacks on Iran threaten the Strait of Hormuz, oil ...

items.description:
Multiple U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded that Iran is not inclined to enter serious negotiations to end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to officials familiar with the assessments, dimming hopes for a near-term reopening of the world's most critical energy chokepoint and keeping global oil markets on edge.[1]

The assessments, reported by The New York Times, indicate that Tehran perceives itself as being in a strong position and sees no need to comply with American demands, even as the conflict enters its sixth week. The intelligence findings land as President Trump's April 6 deadline for Iran to reopen the strait draws near, with no clear diplomatic pathway in sight.[2][3][1]
